title: Establish weighted SLO contracts, burst envelopes, and canary exit criteria for conversational & embedding workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines exact SLO contracts (latency envelopes, availability targets, and error budgets) for interactive conversational generation and batch embeddings, and codifies canary exit/abort conditions and staged rollout gates. The goal is a prescriptive operational contract that Product, SRE, and Runtime Engineering can implement and test: 1) measurable SLOs per workload class, 2) weighted burn-rate and burst-handling envelopes, and 3) automated canary decision logic tied to observability signals.
background: We have many overlapping SLO PRDs (latency bands, rollout gates) but lack a single canonical contract that: 1) specifies per-workload quantiles and availability targets, 2) defines how bursty tenant traffic is accounted for, and 3) standardizes canary abort rules for staged releases (hosted and dedicated paths). This causes inconsistent rollouts and manual checks during deploys.
requirements: Define per-workload SLOs: conversational (streaming first-token and per-token), text-generation (non-streaming), and embeddings (batch & async)
Specify P50/P90/P95/P99 latency targets and percent-of-requests coverage for each workload class
Define availability target (monthly) and a clearly computed error budget mechanism
Establish burst envelope policy: short-window allowance, smoothing window, and weighting rules for tenant bursts
Provide canonical canary guardrail thresholds (burn-rate, p99 degradation, error rise) and minimum sample size/duration
Create automated contract tests and CI checks for SLO computation against synthetic workloads
List required dashboards/alerts and runbook steps for canary abort and rollback
Align with Dedicated and Private deployment constraints (regional fallbacks, no external fallback for private installations)
Document acceptance criteria and signoff owners from Product, SRE, Runtime, and DX (developer experience)
slo_definitions: Conversational - streaming first-token: P50 <= 120ms, P90 <= 350ms, P99 <= 1.2s; target: 98.5% of requests within envelope
Conversational - per-token tail: P90 <= 60ms, P99 <= 160ms; target: 99% of tokens within envelope
Text generation (non-streaming) - full response latency: P50 <= 250ms, P95 <= 900ms, P99 <= 2.5s; target: 97% coverage
Embeddings - sync small-batch (<=8): P95 <= 400ms, P99 <= 1.5s; async/batch throughput objective: 95th percentile completion time <= 5s
Availability: monthly uptime >= 99.95% for hosted API endpoints (SLO scope: control plane + serving runtime path)
Error budget: 1 - uptime_target (e.g., 0.0005 monthly budget). Burn-rate measured daily and aggregated using 24h and 7d windows
Burst envelope: allow 2x baseline qps for 60s sliding window per tenant without immediate SLO violation; sustained >2x for 15m consumes accelerated burn-rate multiplier (x4)
Weighted SLOs: per-tenant weighting scheme for multi-tenant fleets (weight by recent 7d token volume) to avoid noisy small tenants skewing tail metrics
acceptance_criteria: A canonical SLO document reviewed and approved by Product, SRE, Runtime Eng, and DX (email thread + design doc link)
CI contract tests validate SLO computation logic using replayed production traces (passing against defined baselines)
Dashboards created: per-workload SLO panel, burn-rate panel, canary probe panel, and per-tenant anomaly list

Automated canary job implemented that evaluates metrics at 5m cadence and enforces abort when any of the following fire: 24h burn-rate > 3x, p99 latency breach > 2x SLO for >5 minutes, error rate increase > 5x baseline over 10m
Runbook and playbook published with clear owners and escalation path; smoke test checklist for canary traffic injection
Rollout gate implemented in deployment pipeline supporting percent-based ramps, minimum sample size, and automatic halt on abort conditions
Performance regression tests (benchmark harness) show no more than 5% median latency regression vs baseline for canary model/variant
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Validation (dev/staging): implement SLO computation in staging, run synthetic and replayed traces for 48h
Phase 1 - Small canary (1% of traffic, 2h warmup + 4h steady): monitor SLO panels; abort if any canary abort rule triggers
Phase 2 - Ramp (5% -> 20% over 24h): automated percent ramps with 15m observation windows between steps; manual hold at 20% for 12h
Phase 3 - Global rollout (50% -> 100% over 48h): weighted ramping by region and tenant weight; regional fallbacks available for Hosted; Dedicated scheduled separately
Canary exit criteria: pass automated checks for 24h at current ramp step, burn-rate < 1.5x baseline, no persistent p99 degradation
Abort behavior: immediate rollback to previous stable variant; trigger incident runbook and notify on-call SRE + PM
Post-rollout: 7d observation window with elevated monitoring and a postmortem template pre-filled for any degradation
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Small-tenants with sporadic large requests inflate p99 metrics. Mitigation: apply weighted SLOs and exclude known test tenants from production SLO calculations
Risk: Burst envelope may be abused by noisy tenants. Mitigation: enforce tenant-level throttles and incorporate billing/contractation signals for sustained overuse
Risk: Canary sample size too small leads to false negatives. Mitigation: set minimum sample requirements and synthetic traffic probes to augment low-traffic canaries
Risk: Monitoring gaps for Private deployments. Mitigation: provide a portable SLO exporter and local dashboard templates for on-prem customers
Risk: Implementation drift across teams (Console vs Runtime). Mitigation: CI contract tests and a shared spec repo; mandatory cross-team signoff
implementation_notes: Runtime changes: add per-tenant sliding-window qps counters and burn-rate calculator (work with ENG long-term backlog)
Console: SLO panels must support tenant scoping and weighted views; add canary probe widget and automated abort toggle
SRE: create alerting rules with pre-defined escalation (PagerDuty) and attach runbook to alerts
DX: update API docs to include new SLO contract language and examples for embedding/streaming expectations
Deliverables: canonical SLO doc (this ticket), CI contract tests, dashboard PRs, runbook, and deployment pipeline gate change requests
